title: Benefit Plan Standard: Pharmacy Module
description: Draft (v0.2.3) of the pharmacy benefits module for BPS v1.1.0+. A superset of v0.1.0: it carries forward the v0.1.0 structural layer (top-level `pharmacy` object with formulary tiers, pharmacy networks, Medicare Part D coverage stages, and pharmacy-specific accumulators; plus optional `benefits[]` extension fields) and adds the drug-level formulary layer: `pharmacy.formulary_items[]` (drug-to-tier mapping with utilization-management flags), `coverage_exceptions[]` (indication-dependent coverage, the part FHIR DaVinci FormularyItem cannot express), a `formulary_reference` provenance object with public plan join keys, and an optional canonical `tier_code` on formulary tiers. All additions are optional and backward-compatible: a v1.1.0 document, or a v0.1.0 pharmacy document, continues to validate. v0.2.2 adds pharmacy.deductible.family_amount, and a v0.2.1 document validates unchanged. v0.2.3 (the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9) makes room for the CMS monthly Part D formulary files: formulary_reference.formulary_version and formulary_items_url; on formulary_item, coverage_basis, negotiation_selected_drug, capped_benefit and source_references (with a copy of the core schema's source_reference in $defs); and formulary_item.drug_name and quantity_limit_detail.units become optional, since those files name no drug and give no unit. A v0.2.2 document validates unchanged. NOT yet normative; published for community review.

pharmacy.description: Plan-level pharmacy benefit definitions. Optional. When present, `benefits[]` items with `benefit_type: "pharmacy"` may reference its formulary_tiers, pharmacy_networks, and coverage_stages, and `formulary_items[]` may carry the drug-level formulary.

formulary_tiers.description: Drug formulary tiers (e.g., generic, preferred brand, non-preferred brand, specialty). Order is preserved.

pharmacy_networks.description: Pharmacy network tiers (e.g., preferred retail, standard retail, mail order, specialty pharmacy). A separate concept from the medical `network_tiers[]`.

coverage_stages.description: Coverage stages, primarily for Medicare Part D plans. Post-2025 (IRA redesign): Deductible, Initial Coverage, Catastrophic Coverage. The pre-2025 Coverage Gap (donut hole) remains representable for historical plan years. Commercial plans may omit this.

formulary_items.description: Optional drug-level formulary. Each entry places a drug on a formulary tier and carries utilization-management flags and optional indication-dependent coverage. Optional because many plans publish tier structure without a full drug list. This is structure for drug data; adopters supply their own formularies.

formulary_reference.description: Provenance and identity metadata for the plan's formulary data.

formulary_version.description: The version of the formulary the items were read from, as its source names it (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9). The CMS Part D formulary files give each FORMULARY_ID a FORMULARY_VERSION, and the list under 1 id can change from 1 monthly file to the next. Absent or null means the source names no version.

formulary_items_url.description: Where the plan's drug list is published as a formulary list document (schema/v1.2.0/formulary.schema.json), for a list that many plans share and that is written once (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9). A URI, or a reference relative to this document. The plan's drug list is then the list's formulary_items together with this document's own pharmacy.formulary_items, and an item here replaces a list item with the same rxcui and coverage_basis. The list carries no tiers: its formulary_tier_id values name tiers in this document's pharmacy.formulary_tiers. Absent or null means the plan's drug list, if it has one, is pharmacy.formulary_items alone.

source_plan_identifiers.description: Public identifiers used to join external formulary data to this plan. They name the plan the formulary file was read for, which can differ from the document's own plan_identifiers, so they stay pharmacy-scoped.

source_type.description: Origin of this data source. `sbc_extraction` / `spd_extraction`: extracted from the plan's SBC or SPD. `cms_qhp_formulary` / `cms_part_d_formulary`: a CMS machine-readable formulary file. `fhir_davinci_formulary`: a payer Da Vinci PDex Formulary API. `carrier_formulary_document` (v0.2.1): a carrier-published formulary document such as a medication guide, a prior-authorization program list, a program drug list, or a pharmacy policy bulletin; identify the document with `source_url` and `file_date`. `carrier_api`: a carrier or PBM API other than FHIR. `manual_entry`: keyed in by a person.

deductible.description: Pharmacy-specific deductible (separate from the medical deductible). Common in Medicare Part D and tiered commercial plans.

family_amount.description: Family pharmacy deductible, when the plan prints one beside the individual amount (v1.2.0 draft 7; the GatorCare Prime EPO 2026 pharmacy SBC, '$125 Individual/$500 Family Pharmacy Calendar Year Deductible'). amount then holds the individual amount. Absent or null means the document states no family amount, which is the reading before v1.2.0 draft 7.

applies_to_tiers.description: List of formulary tier_ids the deductible applies to. If omitted, applies to all tiers.

out_of_pocket_max.description: Pharmacy-specific OOP max, if separate from the integrated medical OOP max. Most plans use an integrated OOP max; this field is for plans that don't.

mail_order_supply_multiplier.description: When mail-order is a 90-day supply for the cost of N retail copays, this is N. Common values: 2.0 (90 for 2x30) or 2.5. Use day_supply on individual benefit entries for exact representations.

source_reference.description: A citation back to the source document: a page and an excerpt. Used by the plan-level source_references and, since v1.2.0 (gap G14 of the Medicare Advantage notes), by benefits[].source_references. Since v1.2.0 draft 9 also by pharmacy.formulary_items[].source_references and by a formulary list document's source_references (schema/v1.2.0/formulary.schema.json); the pharmacy module v0.2.3 carries a copy of this shape.

document.description: Which source document the citation is in, when the plan was read from more than 1 (v1.2.0 draft 7; GatorCare Prime EPO 2026 has a medical SBC and a pharmacy SBC, each with its own page 4). A file name, a URL or other label the publisher chooses. Absent or null means the plan's 1 source document, which is the reading before v1.2.0 draft 7.

drug_class.description: Canonical drug class. Recommended values: 'preferred_generic', 'generic', 'preferred_brand', 'nonpreferred_brand', 'preferred_specialty', 'nonpreferred_specialty', 'preventive'. See vocabularies/canonical-benefits.json pharmacy category for the cross-reference.

tier_code.description: Optional canonical tier code from the FHIR DrugTierVS vocabulary (e.g. 'generic', 'preferred-brand', 'specialty'). Complements the carrier-facing `drug_class`. Adopters may populate either or both; `drug_class` stays the human/source value, `tier_code` the canonical cross-walk target.

default_day_supply.description: Default day supply for this network (e.g., 30 retail, 90 mail-order).

stage_id.description: Plan-defined identifier. Medicare Part D canonical values (post-2025 redesign): 'DEDUCTIBLE', 'INITIAL', 'CATASTROPHIC'. 'COVERAGE_GAP' remains valid for plan years before 2025.

stage_type.description: Recommended Medicare Part D values (post-2025 redesign): 'deductible', 'initial', 'catastrophic'. 'coverage_gap' remains valid for plan years before 2025. Commercial plans may use other values.

applies_before_total_drug_cost.description: Total-drug-cost ceiling at which this stage ends (Medicare Part D).

applies_after_total_out_of_pocket.description: Total-OOP threshold at which this stage begins (Medicare Part D catastrophic).

quantity_limit_detail.description: A pharmacy quantity limit. Shared shape, referenced by the per-benefit extension, by `formulary_item`, and by an indication-level `restrictions_override`.

units.description: e.g., 'tablets', 'capsules', 'mL', 'doses', 'pens'. Optional since v0.2.3 (the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9): the CMS Part D formulary files give a quantity limit as an amount and a number of days, with no unit. Absent means the source states no unit.

formulary_item.description: A single drug placed on a formulary tier, with utilization-management flags and optional indication-dependent coverage.

rxcui.description: RxNorm Concept Unique Identifier. Primary drug identifier; required when the item is populated.

drug_name.description: Human-readable drug name. Optional since v0.2.3 (the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9): the CMS Part D formulary files identify a drug by RXCUI and NDC and name none, and rxcui identifies the drug. Absent means the source names no drug.

covered.description: Default coverage status when no coverage_exception matches.

coverage_exceptions.description: Indication-dependent overrides on the default coverage. Empty/absent = the `covered` value applies in all indications.

coverage_basis.description: Which program pays for this drug (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9), with the recommended values of benefits[].coverage_basis in the core schema: 'medicare_covered' for a drug covered under Medicare Part D (a row of the CMS Basic Drugs Formulary file), 'supplemental_mandatory' for a drug that Part D excludes and the plan covers as a supplemental benefit every member gets (a row of the CMS Excluded Drugs Formulary file, which enhanced alternative plans may elect to cover). Not enforced as enum. A plan can list the same rxcui twice, once per coverage_basis: the contract year 2027 CMS files have 43 such plan rows. Absent or null means the document does not make the distinction.

negotiation_selected_drug.description: true when the drug is one of the Part D drugs selected for negotiation under the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, as the CMS Part D formulary files flag it (SELECTED_DRUG_YN) (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9). Absent or null means the source does not say.

capped_benefit.description: true when the source flags a capped benefit restriction on the drug, as the CMS Excluded Drugs Formulary file does (CAPPED_BENEFIT_YN) with no amount (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9). Absent or null means the source does not say.

source_references.description: Citations for this item's values, the shape of benefits[].source_references in the core schema (v0.2.3; the Benefit Plan Standard 1.2.0 draft 9). For an item read from a CMS formulary file: the row it was read from.

coverage_exception.description: An indication-specific override on a formulary item's default coverage. Models the same drug having different coverage by clinical indication (e.g. a GLP-1 covered for type 2 diabetes, excluded for weight management, covered-with-restrictions for cardiovascular risk reduction). No equivalent exists in FHIR DaVinci FormularyItem.

indication_code.description: ICD-10-CM code (or other code-system value) for the indication.

formulary_tier_id_override.description: A different pharmacy.formulary_tiers[].tier_id that applies for this indication.

restrictions_override.description: PA/ST/QL flags that override the item-level defaults for this indication.

conditions.description: Human-readable coverage conditions (e.g. 'documented ASCVD; BMI criteria may apply').

formulary_alternative.description: A suggested alternative drug for a formulary item (e.g. a preferred therapeutic equivalent).

rxcui.description: RxNorm Concept Unique Identifier of the alternative drug.

drug_name.description: Human-readable name of the alternative drug.

formulary_tier_id.description: References pharmacy.formulary_tiers[].tier_id, if the alternative is on this plan's formulary.

pharmacy_benefit_extension.description: Optional extension fields on `benefits[]` items when `benefit_type` is 'pharmacy'. These reference into the top-level `pharmacy` object. To use, add these fields directly to a benefit item alongside the standard core-schema fields.

pharmacy_network_id.description: References `pharmacy.pharmacy_networks[].network_id`. Useful when the same drug tier has different cost shares at different pharmacy networks.

coverage_stage_id.description: References `pharmacy.coverage_stages[].stage_id`. For Medicare Part D plans, you typically have one benefit entry per (tier, network, stage) combination.

day_supply.description: Day supply this cost-share applies to (e.g., 30, 90).

drug_examples.description: Optional list of example drug names commonly in this tier. For documentation only; not authoritative. For an authoritative drug list, use `pharmacy.formulary_items[]`.

step_therapy_required.description: Whether step therapy applies before this drug is covered.
